_note: The five rarity tiers: how often each is drawn, and what it looks like. Weight is relative within a draw before luck is applied; `luckScaling` is how much a point of luck pushes toward that tier, so luck makes good cards likelier without ever making commons impossible. Colour and rank are the visual contract the UI renders — one place, so a tier means the same thing on a level-up card, a shop card and a Homestead card.
_designNote: Order matters: tiers are listed commonest first and the UI may rely on that for sorting.
_redesign: Replaces the placeholder palette. `glow` and `badge` are GONE — the rosette and the tier-only glow are not part of the design any more. A tier is now a stamped tin plate riveted across the bottom of the card's art window: `colour` is the plate's top stop, `dark` its bottom stop, `ink` its text, and `rank` the number of diamond pips flanking the tier name (1-5). The tier name is spelled out on the plate, so colour is never the only channel — the word and the pip count both survive greyscale. Only Legendary animates (a foil sweep across the plate), which is why the sweep means one thing.
_epicColour: Epic ships red per the standard genre ladder (grey/green/blue/red/orange). If red reads too close to the damage red in the HUD, the tested alternative is violet: colour #9b6bc8, dark #563579, ink #f6ecff. Changing it here changes it everywhere.
